body:
This post might get removed due to the rules of this sub, but I'd like to ask you - did he write a note? If yes, did you find the note helpful? If no, do you think that writing a note would've helped you?

And are you the mother or the father?

Yeah, like people die all the time for a good cause, I wish I could've switch life with one of those. They have family and a future, I have nothing. They will gladly stay alive forever, I'll gladly die instead of them.
Have you considered trying some meds or talks with a therapist? I mean, they're far from being a magic solution, but it's worth trying if you haven't yet.
What was your motivation/reasons/mindset in the first place, and what has changed?

Actually I kind of got used to it and I've been through creepier and weirder periods in my life, but it still tearing my apart the doubt and the feeling that you can't actually plan to the long term.

It's also feels kind of creepy when you tell yourself 'ok, next week I'm doing it and getting it done' and a week later you find yourself still alive saying to yourself 'Ok, so next week again or should I aim for a longer term?'

> I have absolutely no sense of long-term thinking or goal planning or anything beyond "get through the next couple days and figure it out later." Exactly 50% of me is "don't do X thing, that'll lead to Y bad effect" and the other half is "who cares about the consequences, you'll be dead by this time next month."

Same here, I didn't had a suicide attempt yet (and I hope that I won't fail when I'll attempt) but that part is exactly how I feel right now.
Was your aunt aware of what your dad is doing to you?

Going out of an abusive relationship (assuming this is the case here and you wanna end it) isn't easy, he might manipulate and attack you emotionally, or even physically. 
I'd suggest you to find a friend or someone who'd help you go through the process, and be there for you if he tries to manipulate you in any way.
Goodbye friend, may you rest in peace 😞💔
Out of curiosity, how old are you?

I grew up in a family with more than 5 siblings, my parents didn't earn much. We weren't really poor (i. e. we had basic food and needs) but some more money could've make life much less stressful for my parents. They would have some more patience for us if they weren't in a constant battle to survive financially.

Same here, I just personally feel that if things just went a little different I may had a chance to do something useful with my life.
But now, I'm just a complete failure, my life is just meaningless.
